summary: Post-Monday fix round: tip pools + tax invoices per company, kitchen/admin consistency, books guards + catch-up, bookings/SMTP/fiscal screens, cancelled-ticket card refunds — build, adversarial review, fix

built.summary:
Stream D is done and all three items are fixed. Tip pools and tax invoices now each store their own company. Staff with no login can be tip pool members. The tip-pool outlier and CapEx over-budget alerts have their own kinds.

(1) Tip pools (HR-R7):
- TipPool has a tenantId column (NOT NULL, indexed on tenantId + periodStart).
- Routes use the tenantScope helpers:
  - Lists use the read scope.
  - Edit, post, pay, delete and member routes use the write scope; a pool of another company is 404.
  - Create binds to the active company. A brand of another of the operator's companies gets 422 BRAND_NOT_IN_COMPANY; a brand of a company they are not in gets 404.
- Every fallback to the operator's company is gone. The pool's own company now decides its payout journal, audit rows and exception flags.
- TipPoolMember: userId is now nullable and there is a new employeeId (FK to HrEmployee, indexed). A CHECK constraint (tip_pool_members_one_person) makes sure exactly one of the two is set. Uniqueness per pool is two partial unique indexes written in SQL; they are deliberately not declared in schema.prisma. Prisma 5.22's migrate diff does not see partial indexes, so declaring them would make the next generated migration create them again. The model carries a comment explaining this.
- The member builder now includes staff with no login, read from the company's attendance punches. Their tip-pool role comes from their HR designation or, failing that, their department (new hrRoleKey: barista, cashier, expediter, foh, kitchen).
- If neither says a role, that person is listed with the new reason 'no_role'. Posting is refused with 409 STAFF_ROLE_UNKNOWN until they are added with a weight or left out by name with a reason (audited).
- The KIOSK_STAFF_NOT_IN_POOL stop-gap is removed. The post body field is now leaveOutStaff; the old name leaveOutKioskStaff is still accepted.
- New routes: GET /tip-pools/:id/candidates and POST /tip-pools/:id/members. A member from another company gets 422 MEMBER_NOT_IN_COMPANY; a member already in the pool gets 409; a role with no weight gets 422 ROLE_WEIGHT_REQUIRED. An employee who has a login is stored by that login, the same way the builder does it.
- Posting also re-checks that every member still belongs to the pool's company (422).
- Payout: one journal entry per pool in the pool's company (Dr 2095 / Cr a cash or bank account of that company). Each member's share, for login holders and no-login staff alike, is recorded on their member row with a name snapshot and its own tippool.distribute audit row. Tips are not paid through payroll.
- Unchanged rules: pay only from the company's cash or bank accounts, and not while a till holding tips from the window is open or not yet on the books.
- Admin tip-pools page:
  - shows "no login" and the employee code on such members;
  - asks for a weight for each person with no known role and has an "Add to pool" button;
  - can add anyone from the pool's company to a draft;
  - the paid label no longer uses the check-mark glyph.

(2) Tax invoices:
- TaxInvoice has a tenantId column (NOT NULL, FK, index on tenantId + issuedAt). The global unique on invoiceNumber is replaced by @@unique([tenantId, invoiceNumber]).
- Today's numbering had four faults: it used one counter per brand in invoice_counters; invoices and credit notes shared that counter; a new year started at 2; and two brands with the same prefix collided.
- New numbering is per (company, prefix, Karachi year, invoice or credit note). It takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock on the series, then reads the highest existing number and adds one, in READ COMMITTED. It is race-safe and gap-free, and the one-invoice-per-order check runs under the same lock.
- Credit notes take the original invoice's company and use their own -CN- series.
- invoices/routes.ts now uses scopeTenantWhere and conceptWhere: reads use the read scope, issuing a document needs the order to be in the write scope, and anything foreign is 404.
- invoice_counters is no longer read.

(3) Alert kinds:
- Added 'tip_pool_outlier' and 'capex_over_budget' to lib/exceptions.ts, plus STAND_IN_KINDS and kindsMatching().
- The CapEx de-dup query matches both the old stand-in 'high_value_void' and the new kind, so open flags are not raised twice.
- The tip-pool migration re-kinds old rows by their exact titles and entity types.
- Added labels to KIND_LABEL on the admin exceptions page.
- Also removed the `as never` cast on the flag's metadata write (it now writes Prisma.DbNull).

Both migrations were run against a database built from the old schema with sample rows. Every backfill branch, both NOTICEs, the re-kind, the CHECK constraint, the partial unique indexes and a re-run all behaved as intended. Afterwards prisma migrate diff against the new schema showed an empty migration.

items.note: TipPool.tenantId added, with a backfill in the order you asked for: the brand's company, then the creator's company, then the one company all members' logins belong to, then the oldest active company with a NOTICE per pool. Routes use read, write and create scopes; every operator-company fallback is removed; the pool's own company decides its journal entry, audit rows and flags. TipPoolMember now takes userId or employeeId, exactly one (CHECK), with two partial unique indexes. Staff with no login are built from attendance punches, with their role taken from their HR designation or department. Anyone with no known role must be added with a weight or left out by name. The 409 KIOSK_STAFF_NOT_IN_POOL stop-gap is removed. New add-member and candidates routes, both requiring the member to be in the pool's company (422). Shares are recorded per member row plus one journal entry per pool, not through payroll. Admin page updated. Two-company tests cover: company B gets 404 on A's pool, create binds to the active company, A's pool cannot take B's employee or login, and an employee member gets a share and the payout posts balanced in the pool's company.

TaxInvoice.tenantId added (backfilled from the brand's company; credit notes take the original's; NOTICE fallback), NOT NULL, foreign key, indexed. The unique is now per company. Numbering is per (company, prefix, Karachi year, invoice or credit note) under an advisory lock; today's per-brand counter is replaced (it shared one sequence between invoices and credit notes, restarted a year at 2, and collided across brands with the same prefix). Routes use the tenantScope helpers; foreign is 404. Tests: the same prefix in two companies gives A's #1 and B's #1; B gets 404 everywhere on A's invoice; a concurrent pair and 10 at once in one company get distinct numbers with no gaps; the same order issued twice at once gives one invoice; credit-note series; Karachi year.

Added 'tip_pool_outlier' and 'capex_over_budget' plus kindsMatching(). The CapEx de-dup matches both the new kind and the old stand-in. The tip-pool migration re-kinds old rows WHERE kind='high_value_void' AND entityType='TipPool' AND title LIKE 'Tip pool: % taking %', and entityType='CapexProject' AND title LIKE 'CapEx project over budget: %'. Labels added to KIND_LABEL. Tests cover the new kind, a single raise, an open old-kind flag still de-duping, and the pool's company on the outlier flag.

built.prodNotes:
Deploy order: the API image and both migrations ship together. Run `prisma migrate deploy` before the new API serves traffic, because the new code writes tenantId and employeeId. Both migrations only add, backfill and re-index, and they are safe to re-run. Migration 20261012120000 must run before 20261012120100 (timestamp order already does this).

Watch the deploy log for NOTICEs:
- 'tip_pool_company: pool … assigned to the oldest active company …': a pool with no brand, no creator company and members spread over several companies. Each such pool is named with its window and amount. Check each one and move it with `UPDATE tip_pools SET "tenantId"=…` if it is wrong.
- 'tax_invoice_company: invoice … brand … has no company': none are expected. A RAISE EXCEPTION happens only if rows exist and there is no company at all.

Row-level security: the tip_pools policy is replaced. It now checks "tenantId" = ANY(app_tenant_ids()); previously a pool with a null conceptId was visible to every staff session. The tax_invoices policy is unchanged (it is the generic order-chain policy).

Existing exception flags: open tip-pool outlier and CapEx over-budget flags are re-kinded from 'high_value_void' by title, so the inbox shows the right label and they stop inflating the high-value-void count.

Tip pools in progress:
- A draft computed before the deploy that a no-login staff member worked on will now show that person as 'missing' (if their designation gives a role) or under 'Staff with no known tip-pool role'. Delete the draft and compute it again, or add them with a weight.
- Posted and paid pools are untouched.

Tax invoices: the next invoice in each (company, prefix, year) series continues from the highest number already issued in that series. Credit notes now have their own -CN- sequence instead of taking numbers from the invoice counter. The year is the Karachi calendar year (it was the UTC year). invoice_counters is left in place but no longer read; it can be dropped in a later cleanup.

Rollback: an older API image would fail to issue invoices for an order whose (prefix, year) number already exists in another company. It would also try to write tip pools without tenantId, which the NOT NULL column refuses, so tip pool creation fails until re-deployed. Do not roll back below this release without reverting the migrations.
built.ownerQuestions:
1. Staff with no login get their tip-pool role from their HR designation or department, matched by keyword: cook/chef/kitchen/prep/dish/helper/grill/tandoor → kitchen (0.5), waiter/server/host → foh (1.0), cashier → 0.75, barista → 0.75, expediter → 0.5. Anyone else (for example "Security Guard") blocks posting until an approver adds them with a weight or leaves them out by name. Is that the rule you want, or should an unknown role default to the kitchen weight?
2. Tip shares are paid as one cash or bank payout per pool, with each person's share recorded on their member row. They do not go through payroll or payslips. Should tip shares appear on the HR payslip in a later round?

review.title: Staff with no login: the department fallback in hrRoleKey uses keywords that match too much, so non-tip staff get a share without anyone being asked
review.scenario: hrRoleKey (~line 175) checks the designation first, then the department, with loose patterns: /service/ and /host/ map to foh (weight 1.0) and /helper/ maps to kitchen. A designation the patterns don't recognise falls through to the department. I reproduced this on servd_test_r5_d_rv through the real routes. Company A has a server with a login (4 h) and a security guard with no login: designation 'Security Guard', department 'Security Services', 4 h of kiosk punches at the branch. POST /tip-pools created the guard as a member at weight 1, 4 units. Review blockers and staffWithoutRole were both empty. POST /post paid the guard PKR 150 of a PKR 300 pot. The builder's report and owner question 1 say a Security Guard 'blocks posting', but here it does not. Direct hrRoleKey checks gave: ('Security Guard','Admin & Services') → foh, ('Accountant','Finance Services') → foh, ('Office Boy','Customer Service') → foh, ('Plumber','Hospitality Services') → foh, ('Ghost Kitchen Driver', null) → foh (because 'Ghost' contains 'host'), ('Maintenance Helper', ...) → kitchen, ('Electrician Helper', null) → kitchen. In each case tips move from the real tip staff to someone outside the pool, with no prompt and no flag. The 40% outlier flag does not catch it.
review.fix: Match whole words and drop the broad keywords: remove 'service' and bare 'helper', and match host as \bhost(ess)?\b. Do not fall back to the department when the designation is set but unrecognised. Only use the department when there is no designation, and then only for exact department names (Kitchen, Main Kitchen, FOH, Front of House, BOH). Better still, add an explicit role mapping on HrOrgUnit/designation, so the 'no_role' prompt is the default for anything not listed. Add regression tests: 'Security Guard'/'Security Services' → null (posting refused with STAFF_ROLE_UNKNOWN), 'Ghost Kitchen Driver' → null, 'Maintenance Helper' → null.

review.title: An HR employee whose login was soft-deleted is dropped from the pool without a word, and their share goes to the others
review.scenario: In hoursAtBrand (~line 224), the emps query only takes employees with userId in the live users set (users.deletedAt IS NULL) or with userId NULL. When the CEO deletes a login, auth/routes.ts sets deletedAt but leaves HrEmployee.userId in place, so that employee matches neither branch. Their attendance is never read, they are not in 'worked', they are not 'excluded', and they are not 'missing'. I reproduced this: employee 'Kamran Cook', designation Line Cook, linked to a soft-deleted boh login, with 4 h of attendance at the branch. The created pool held only the guard and the server, the review was clean, and posting split the whole pot without him. HR-R7 promises staff with no working login are pool members and that hours are 'never dropped silently'. Neither holds for this person. The kiosk refuses him (HAS_LOGIN), so his hours come from HR-entered or corrected attendance. The same gap covers an HR record in company A linked to a login that is neither based in A nor a member of A.
review.fix: In hoursAtBrand, treat an employee whose userId is not in the live users set as no-login staff. Select HrEmployee rows with attendance where userId IS NULL OR userId NOT IN (live userIds), and put them through the no-login branch: role from hrRoleKey, stored as an employeeId member. This matches what POST /:id/members already does for a deleted login (it stores employeeId when the user lookup returns null). Add a regression test with a soft-deleted login.

review.title: Invoice numbering scans every invoice the company has ever issued while holding the series lock, so issuing slows down every year
review.scenario: nextNumber (~line 57) runs SELECT MAX(CAST(SUBSTRING(...))) WHERE tenantId=$1 AND type::text=$2 AND LEFT(invoiceNumber,n)=head AND SUBSTRING(...) ~ '^[0-9]+$'. LEFT() and the regex cannot use an index, so Postgres reads every invoice of the company, from all years and all prefixes. It does this inside pg_advisory_xact_lock for the series. issueInvoiceForOrder runs automatically on every completed order (orders/service.ts ~2253). I measured it on servd_test_r5_d_rv with 300k invoices in one company: EXPLAIN ANALYZE showed a Bitmap Heap Scan over all 300,016 rows, 127 ms, using tax_invoices_tenantId_issuedAt_idx. That caps one brand prefix at about 8 invoices per second, and the cap falls as the company's history grows, because every completion waits on the lock. Each waiter holds a pool connection, and the interactive transaction has Prisma's default 5 s timeout with no timeout option set. In a rush (for example a batch of till closes, or a busy brand after a year or two), queued issues fail with P2028. The failure is only logged as '[invoice] auto-issue failed', so customer tax invoices go missing until someone issues them by hand. The old per-brand invoice_counters row was O(1).
review.fix: Keep a counter per series. Add a table such as tax_invoice_series(tenantId, head, nextValue) with @@unique([tenantId, head]) (a stream D schema change). Allocate with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenantId, head) DO UPDATE SET nextValue = tax_invoice_series.nextValue + 1 RETURNING nextValue, seeded once from today's MAX in the migration. The row lock gives the same race-safety and gap-free guarantee. Do not switch to ORDER BY invoiceNumber DESC LIMIT 1: the numbers are padded to 5 digits and become 6 digits after 99,999, and text ordering then gets them wrong. Whatever the approach, pass an explicit { timeout, maxWait } to the $transaction.

review.title: A no-login staff member with no known role and punches at an unknown branch blocks posting, and leaving them out by name does not clear it
review.scenario: Take a company with several brands, for example GS Foods with Simmer, Stackd and Flipd. A no-login security guard (role null) kiosk-punches with no geofence match and has no HR branch. hoursAtBrand marks the spans 'unknown' and excludes them as no_branch, with 0 worked hours, so computePool never adds a no_role entry for them. The `relevant` filter (`!x.userId && x.role == null`) keeps the no_branch row, so reviewDraft adds a blocker: '<name>: N h not counted — no branch is known...'. leaveOutStaff only clears staffWithoutRole (reason 'no_role'), so naming the guard with a reason has no effect. POST /post stays 409 POOL_NOT_READY until HR sets the guard's branch, even though the guard is not in the tip pool. The same happens for an open shift ('still_on_shift'). Before this change, a kiosk worker's unknown-place hours were grouped under 'no_login', and the approver could leave them out by name.
review.fix: For no-login staff with role null, report unknown-place and open hours as reason 'no_role' (summed with any placed hours), or let leaveOutStaff also clear no_branch and still_on_shift rows for employeeIds with role null. That way an approver can still record by name that someone outside the pool (a guard) is not in it.

fix.summary:
I checked all four review findings against the uncommitted stream D changes. All four were real, so all four are fixed with regression tests and none was rejected.

D-RV-1: hrRoleKey in backend/src/modules/tipPools/routes.ts now matches whole words only. A list of jobs that are never tip roles (driver, rider, delivery, security, guard, maintenance, electrician, plumber, accountant, office, admin, cleaner and similar) returns null even when the title also contains a tip word, so 'Ghost Kitchen Driver' and 'Maintenance Helper' are null. The broad keywords 'service', bare 'helper', bare 'kitchen' and bare 'host' are gone. Host is now matched as host or hostess, and kitchen only as 'kitchen helper/hand/assistant/porter/staff'. If a designation is set but not recognised, the result is null and the department is not read. The department is used only when there is no designation, and then only for these exact names: Kitchen, Main Kitchen, BOH, Back of House, FOH, Front of House.

D-RV-2: hoursAtBrand now reads every HR employee with attendance in the company. Anyone whose userId is not a live login of that company is treated as staff with no login (a new noLogin() helper): a deleted login, or a login that is not of this company. They become employeeId members with their role from hrRoleKey. This matches what POST /:id/members already does.

D-RV-4: in computePool, all of a no-login, unknown-role person's hours in the window are now folded into one 'no_role' row. That includes hours placed at the brand, hours with no known branch, and hours on a shift still open. So they no longer produce a no_branch or still_on_shift blocker that leaveOutStaff could never clear. The approver either adds them on the draft or leaves them out by name. The rule for login holders' unplaced hours is unchanged and has a test.

D-RV-3: numbering now uses a new TaxInvoiceSeries table (tax_invoice_series, primary key (tenantId, head), column lastValue). One INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING inside the issuing transaction gives the next number. It is race-safe because of the row lock, and gap-free because a rolled-back issue rolls its number back. The advisory series lock stays, so the one-invoice-per-order check still runs under it.

There is also a one-time catch-up. After allocating, the service checks the unique (tenantId, invoiceNumber) index to see whether the number is already taken, for example by an older release issuing mid-deploy. If it is, the counter jumps once to the highest number issued in that series, found by number shape. Both transactions now pass an explicit { maxWait: 10s, timeout: 20s }.

The migration 20261012120100 creates the table and seeds it from existing numbers by their shape, not their type. This matters because the old per-brand counter gave credit notes invoice-shaped numbers. The seed can be re-run safely and only ever raises a value. I tested it on a scratch database shaped like the old schema, where it seeded 42 including a legacy credit note numbered 'STX-2026-00042'.

Measured on 300k invoices in one company: the old MAX query took 63 ms (a parallel scan of every row of the table). The new upsert takes 0.25 ms and the index check 0.02 ms.

The READMEs for tipPools and invoices are updated. wipe-and-reset.ts now also clears tax_invoice_series, so numbering restarts along with the invoices.

items.note: hrRoleKey: whole-word tip roles, a list of non-tip jobs that always gives null, no department fallback when a designation is set, and only exact department names when it is not. Tests: every case the reviewer listed now gives null (Security Guard/Security Services, Accountant, Office Boy, Plumber, Ghost Kitchen Driver, Maintenance Helper, Electrician Helper), and Supervisor/Kitchen gives null. End to end in company C, the guard is not a member, staffWithoutRole lists him, POST /post returns 409 STAFF_ROLE_UNKNOWN, and with leaveOutStaff the pot goes to the server and the cook only. The audit metadata records who was left out and the reason.

hoursAtBrand reads every HR employee with attendance. Anyone whose userId is not a live login of this company goes through the no-login branch as an employeeId member. Test: 'Kamran Cook' with a soft-deleted boh login and 4 h is a member at weight 0.5 with 2 units, and receives PKR 100 of the PKR 300 pot.

New TaxInvoiceSeries counter table, allocated by one upsert. A taken number triggers a one-time catch-up by number shape. Explicit { maxWait: 10_000, timeout: 20_000 } on both issuing transactions. The migration seed reads numbers by shape (legacy credit notes in invoice shape count). Tests: separate counters per company and per series; the counter decides the number with no MAX over invoices; catch-up past hand-made or legacy numbers with no duplicates; an old credit note in invoice shape is stepped over; the migration seed is run from the SQL file and is re-runnable and never lowers a series. Measured on 300k rows: 63 ms before, 0.27 ms after.

computePool folds a no-login, unknown-role person's no_branch and still_on_shift hours into their single 'no_role' row. Test: a company with two brands, one guard punching with no branch (3 h) and one guard still clocked in (3 h). blockers is empty and both are in staffWithoutRole. Naming only one is refused with 409 naming the other. Naming both posts the full pot to the server.

fix.tests: npx tsc --noEmit -p . in backend passes. I made no frontend changes in this fix round, so the frontend tsc was not needed. I ran vitest against servd_test_r5_d with Redis on 6390/13 and --no-file-parallelism over 11 files: tipPoolCompany (15 tests, 5 new), taxInvoiceCompany (10 tests, 5 new), auditPeopleTips, approvalsInbox, attendanceRota, auditPeopleAccess, fiscalPayload, preBills, receipt, resimPeople and wave3Finance. Result: 11 files and 175 tests passed. The migration 20261012120100 also applied cleanly, twice, to the test database and to a scratch database shaped like the old schema; the scratch database was dropped afterwards.
fix.needsOtherFiles: None required. The new TaxInvoiceSeries model is part of stream D's schema scope, next to TaxInvoice: one model plus one back-relation on Tenant ('TenantTaxInvoiceSeries'). The integrator should know it is a new table in migration 20261012120100.
fix.ownerQuestions: 1) Who counts as a tip role is now deliberately narrow. Staff with no login whose designation is something like 'Steward', 'Captain', 'Food Runner' or 'Supervisor' come up as 'role unknown' on every pool until an approver adds them or leaves them out. Do you want any of those designations to count as front-of-house automatically, or do you want an explicit role setting on the HR designation in a later round? 2) Before go-live, should the old invoice_counters table be dropped? It is no longer read.
fix.prodNotes: Migration 20261012120100 now also creates tax_invoice_series and seeds it from existing invoice numbers. The seed is idempotent and only raises values. If the old API issues invoices between the migration and the container swap, the next number may already be taken. The new code then catches up past it once (one scan, only on that occasion), so no duplicate number and no failed auto-issue. After deploy, the normal issue path never scans tax_invoices.

built.summary:
Stream K is done: all five items are fixed. Backend and admin changes have regression tests; the tablet change has a type check only (no test runner there). The new kitchenConsistency suite (5 tests) and the 8 existing suites that touch these files pass, 158/158. tsc passes for frontend/admin and tablet. Backend tsc fails only in backend/src/modules/tipPools/routes.ts, which another stream is changing right now; none of the errors are in files I touched.

1. Courses reload: GET /orders/:id/courses now returns scheduledFireAt for each line. The Courses page takes the paced lines from the server once the course has fired, so a paced dish still says "fires at HH:MM" after a reload. The last fire response is only used as a stopgap for an older API that lacks the field.
2. Tablet tap on an unfired ticket: OrderTicket has a new itemsTappable prop (default true). The KDS screen sets it to false for NEW-lane tickets, so their lines are disabled, and onItemTap also ignores them as a second guard. Paced lines still show the "Not cooked yet" alert instead of bumping, and fired lines bump as before. lib/orderStateMachine.ts is unchanged.
3. Admin expo page: every emoji is gone (order types, header, Fire button, table chips, warnings, hand-off labels, empty states, the close buttons) and replaced with text labels or small inline SVG icons. All hex and rgba colours, including the old teal-to-indigo gradient on Fire, now use the kds-* Tailwind tokens; the page keeps erp-kitchen-dark with a bg-kds-bg background. Delivery is now kds-blue (there is no kds pink). Pre-orders use kds-subtext.
4. review.title: Tablet KDS: an unfired later-course dish on a FIRED ticket can still be tapped, which marks it done without it being cooked, and its course can then never be fired
review.scenario: Reproduced on DB servd_test_r5_k_rv with a temporary test, since deleted. The order has course 1 (Classic, Fries) and course 2 (Cake). Expo presses Fire, so the ticket moves to the tablet's FIRED lane. /expo/queue returns Cake in that order's items as status 'pending', firedAt null, scheduledFireAt null. Stream K's guard only covers NEW-lane tickets (itemsTappable={t.status !== 'new'}) and paced lines (pacedById, which needs a scheduledFireAt). Cake is neither, so OrderTicket renders it tappable and onItemTap calls PATCH /order-items/:id/status {status:'bumped'}. That call answered 200 and the row became status=bumped with firedAt=null. Then POST /orders/:id/fire-course {course:2} answered 404 NO_ITEMS 'No pending items at course 2'. So the dessert is recorded as done without being cooked, the Courses page can no longer fire it, and the order can reach READY without it. This is the same bug item (2) was meant to fix ('tapping a dish not yet fired marks it done'). It is still there for every later-course line on a fired ticket.
review.fix: Make tappability a per-line rule on the tablet, not a per-ticket one. A line is tappable only if it has actually been fired: it.firedAt != null or it.status !== 'pending'. Add a tappable flag to Ticket.items, set in toTicket, and have OrderTicket disable the Pressable when it is false. That covers the NEW lane, later courses and paced lines with one rule. In onItemTap, keep the paced 'Not cooked yet' alert and add one for an unfired later-course line, e.g. 'Course N has not been fired yet. Fire it from Courses or expo.', instead of bumping. Leave lib/orderStateMachine.ts unchanged. Optionally add a backend test that pins the data shape the tablet relies on: a course-2 line on a fired order has status pending, firedAt null and scheduledFireAt null in /expo/queue.

built.summary:
Stream B is finished. I checked the half-done edits from the stopped attempt and completed them. All 24 tests in the new suite pass, as do the 16 existing suites for these files. Backend tsc has no errors in this stream's files; the only errors are in another stream's file, src/adapters/whatsapp/conversation.ts. Admin tsc is clean.
(1) Purchase orders, bills and payments now refuse any amount over PKR 21,474,836.47 with 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE and a plain message, before anything is written. This covers typed amounts and computed totals.
(2) The CEO can now preview and apply missed bill price differences from the reconciliation page.
(3) A points earn that a refund reversed before its ledger entry landed is no longer posted, and that outcome no longer raises a posting-failed flag.

items.note: Every money input in procurement/routes.ts now goes through one helper that rejects anything over the ceiling. That covers PO and bill unit costs, bill tax, payment amounts, amounts applied to bills, supplier opening balances on create and edit, and the PO approval limit (added in this pass). Quantities must be finite. service.ts checks the same ceiling against every computed total before the database write: each PO line (quantity × unit cost) and the PO total, each bill line plus subtotal, tax and total, and payment amounts. The payment checks are inside createPaymentTx, so the petty-cash path is covered too, and allocatePayment checks before anything moves. The ceiling is the one MAX_LINE_CENTS constant in accounting/journal.ts. reconciliation/service.ts no longer keeps its own copy. Other money paths: bank-statement adjustment split lines now get the same 422 at the input schema. Bank CSV lines were already guarded, and statement balances are BigInt. Receiving stores only a per-unit cost and posts no ledger entry, so it needs no guard.

New action POST /reconciliation/apply-missed-bill-variances with body { dryRun (default true), tenantId? }, for role admin only (others get 403). It runs once for each company in scope. A tenantId outside the caller's scope is 404, and an empty scope is 422. Each row says would_apply, applied, locked or error, with quantity, quantity still on hand, value moved, bill numbers and item name. Running it twice is safe: applied lines are recorded as supplier.bill.variance_applied rows, which count as matched, and each line runs under a lock on its PO, so a second run finds nothing. If a company's books are closed through today, its lines are listed as locked and nothing is applied; a lock added mid-run is caught the same way. A real run shares the backfill's single-flight slot (409 BACKFILL_RUNNING) and writes an audit row only when something changed. On the admin page, MissedBillVariances.tsx sits next to 'Backfill unposted' on the shifts tab: Preview first, then Apply. It uses the colour tokens, has no emoji, and its table scrolls sideways on a phone. Tested with two companies: 404 for a foreign company, the portfolio view covers both, applying for A leaves B untouched, a second run finds nothing, a locked company stays untouched, and the ledger stays balanced.

postLoyaltyEarn and postLoyaltyRedeem now re-read the points transaction under a row lock (FOR UPDATE) inside the posting's own database transaction. If the refund has already reversed it, they stop with reason 'reversed' and post nothing. 'reversed' is now in LOYALTY_NOTHING_TO_POST (exported), so it never raises posting_failed. The reversal path still returns 'original_not_booked' when nothing was booked. If the posting takes the lock first, the refund waits, then finds the entry and reverses it, so the liability account (2060) nets to zero. Both orderings are tested deterministically with real row and advisory locks: nothing is posted for a reversed earn, no flag is raised, the ledger stays balanced, and an earn that was not reversed still posts exactly once.

review.title: A reversed loyalty earn still raises a high posting_failed flag through the order-completion path (ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked)
review.scenario: Reproduced on servd_test_r5_b_rv with a temporary probe. An earn transaction has reversedAt set, which is what postOrderRefund step 1 does when a refund or cancel lands before the earn's ledger entry. Calling ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked(txId, null) returns { posted: false, reason: 'reversed' } and creates 1 posting_failed ExceptionFlag. This is the main order path. completeOrder runs awardOrderPoints → creditPoints → bookEarn, and bookEarn correctly treats 'reversed' as nothing to post. The chained .then(ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked) then calls postLoyaltyEarn again, gets 'reversed', and flags it, because orders/service.ts NOTHING_TO_POST (~line 1948) has no 'reversed'. A refund that interleaves with completion therefore still puts a spurious high 'did not reach the ledger (2060)' exception in the company inbox, which is the outcome item (3) was meant to remove. The builder's summary says 'that outcome no longer raises a posting-failed flag'. That is true only for bookEarn and the backfill. The builder did note the gap under needsOtherFiles. The ledger itself is correct, and a later Backfill-unposted run resolves the flag.
review.fix: In orders/service.ts, import LOYALTY_NOTHING_TO_POST from '../loyalty/service.js' and check it alongside the order-specific reasons (or add 'reversed' and 'not_redeem_tx' to NOTHING_TO_POST). Add a regression test: an earn with reversedAt set → ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked → 0 posting_failed flags.

review.title: Dock receiving without a PO still returns a raw 500 for a unit cost above INT4. The builder's 'receiving needs no guard' claim is wrong
review.scenario: POST /crosschecks/receiving with poId null and a line { inventoryItemId, quantityReceived: 1, unitCostCents: 3000000000 } (photoUrl supplied). The crosschecks schema only checks z.number().int().min(0), and receiveGoods (receiving.ts ~241) only checks that the cost is a non-negative integer. The value reaches goodsReceiptLine.poUnitCostCents and inventoryItem.unitCostCents, both INT4, and Prisma throws 'Unable to fit integer value 3000000000 into an INT4'. That is a raw 500, not 422 AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE. Reproduced by calling receiveGoods directly: the error thrown is not an AppError. The brief asked for the other user-entered money paths under procurement to be checked. The builder dismissed receiving because it 'stores only a per-unit cost', but that stored per-unit cost is the user-typed value on the no-PO dock path.
review.fix: In receiveGoods' no-PO branch, call assertAmountFits(l.unitCostCents, `${it.name}'s unit cost`) from procurement/service.ts. Optionally also put a ceiling on the crosschecks schema. Add a 422 test for the dock-receive route.

review.title: The catch-up's audit row is filed under the operator's home company, not the companies whose books it changed
review.scenario: A CEO who belongs to A and B, with A active and the portfolio view on, runs POST /reconciliation/apply-missed-bill-variances { dryRun: false }. Lines for company B are applied: B's stock is re-priced and 5060 is posted in B's books. The single 'supplier.bill.variance_catch_up' audit row is written with tenantId = req.staffUser.tenantId (A), and its metadata lists B's lines. B's audit trail never shows that the catch-up ran, and A's trail shows B's data. The per-line 'supplier.bill.variance_applied' rows do carry the bill's company, so the amounts can still be traced.
review.fix: Write one audit row per company that had applied rows, with tenantId set to that company and only its rows in metadata. A per-company loop over ran.rows grouped by tenantId does this.

fix.summary:
I checked all three findings against the uncommitted diff, and all three are real. I fixed RV-B-3 in a file I own. RV-B-1 and RV-B-2 are both in files outside stream B (backend/src/modules/orders/service.ts and backend/src/modules/procurement/receiving.ts), so I did not edit them. The exact changes are under needsOtherFiles. For each of those two I added a regression test in backend/tests/booksRound5.test.ts that runs the real path and is marked `it.fails`, so it currently demonstrates the defect. Once the other-file fix is applied, that test will turn red and only needs `it.fails` changed to `it`.

RV-B-3 (fixed, in backend/src/modules/reconciliation/routes.ts): a real run of POST /reconciliation/apply-missed-bill-variances now writes one 'supplier.bill.variance_catch_up' audit row for each company the run touched. Each row is filed under that company and contains only that company's lines: a per-company summary in `after`, and in metadata the company id, its applied lines, and its locked or error lines. Before this, a single row went to the operator's home company and listed every company's lines. A run with nothing to do still writes no audit row.

RV-B-1 (confirmed, not fixed here): orders/service.ts has its own NOTHING_TO_POST list (around line 1948), and it does not include 'reversed'. As a result, ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked raises a high posting_failed flag when an earn was reversed before its entry was booked. The new `it.fails` test reproduces this.

RV-B-2 (confirmed, not fixed here): on dock receiving without a PO, receiveGoods only checks that the unit cost is a non-negative integer. A cost of 3,000,000,000 therefore reaches goodsReceipt.create and Prisma throws a raw error ("Unable to fit integer value '3000000000' into an INT4"), which the API returns as a 500. The new `it.fails` test reproduces that exact error.

items.note: Confirmed by reading the code and by a test: ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked on an earn whose reversedAt is set gets 'reversed' back from postLoyaltyEarn. That reason is not in orders/service.ts NOTHING_TO_POST, so it calls flagPostingFailed. orders/service.ts is not a stream-B file, so the fix is listed under needsOtherFiles. A regression test is in booksRound5.test.ts (3), marked it.fails until that change lands.

Confirmed. receiveGoods (no-PO branch) on a unit cost of 3e9 fails at goodsReceipt.create with the Prisma INT4 conversion error, not with an AppError. receiving.ts and crosschecks/routes.ts are not stream-B files. The PO receive route in procurement/routes.ts is not affected because it uses the PO line cost, which createPo already guards. The fix is under needsOtherFiles. A regression test is in booksRound5.test.ts (4), marked it.fails until that change lands.

reconciliation/routes.ts now writes one audit row per company present in ran.rows, with tenantId set to that company, a per-company summary in `after`, and only that company's applied and not-applied lines in metadata. New two-company test: a CEO in A and B with A active and the portfolio view on applies one line in each company and gets exactly 2 audit rows, one for A and one for B, each naming only its own PO line. B's row is in B's trail even though the operator's home company is A.

fix.tests: Ran against the servd_test_r5_b DB (Redis 6390/15): tests/booksRound5.test.ts, auditReports, booksReconcile, cashDrawer, resimBooks, wave3Finance, auditLedgerLoyalty, loyalty and receiving. All 9 files passed, 142 tests. In booksRound5 that includes the new RV-B-3 two-company audit test and the two `it.fails` tests for RV-B-1 and RV-B-2, which fail for the right reasons: the flagPostingFailed path is hit, and the Prisma INT4 conversion error is thrown. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` in backend shows no errors in my files. The only errors are TS7023 in src/adapters/whatsapp/conversation.ts, which is another stream's uncommitted work. I did not touch any frontend package.
fix.needsOtherFiles:
1) backend/src/modules/orders/service.ts (RV-B-1): add `import { LOYALTY_NOTHING_TO_POST } from '../loyalty/service.js'`. The simplest change is to add 'reversed' and 'not_redeem_tx' to the NOTHING_TO_POST Set (around line 1948), so that every check against NOTHING_TO_POST (postCompletionOrFlag, postRefundOrFlag, ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked) treats them as nothing to post. Alternatively, in ensureLoyaltyEarnBooked only (around line 2030), change the condition to `if (r.reason && !NOTHING_TO_POST.has(r.reason) && !LOYALTY_NOTHING_TO_POST.has(r.reason)) reason = r.reason`. After applying it, change `it.fails('RV-B-1: ...')` to `it(` in backend/tests/booksRound5.test.ts.

2) backend/src/modules/procurement/receiving.ts (RV-B-2): in receiveGoods' no-PO branch, right after the UNIT_COST_REQUIRED check (around line 243), add `assertAmountFits(l.unitCostCents, \`${it.name}'s unit cost\`); assertAmountFits(Math.round(l.unitCostCents * l.quantityReceived), \`${it.name} (quantity × unit cost)\`)`, with `import { assertAmountFits } from './service.js'`. If that import creates a cycle (service.ts does not import receiving.ts today, so it should not), import MAX_LINE_CENTS and amountTooLarge from '../accounting/journal.js' instead. Optionally, also cap the schema in backend/src/modules/crosschecks/routes.ts with `unitCostCents: z.number().int().min(0).max(2_147_483_647)`, keeping the AppError path as the 422 the caller sees. After applying it, change `it.fails('RV-B-2: ...')` to `it(` in backend/tests/booksRound5.test.ts.
